item.title: Measles, dengue double threat puts children at greater risk
item.description:
The simultaneous spread of measles and dengue is exposing children across Bangladesh to a dangerous combination of infections, with doctors warning that patients contracting both diseases face more complicated treatment and potentially life-threatening complications.
The deaths of two brothers, aged 10 years and 10 months, in Chittagong within just two days have brought the growing danger into sharp focus.
The children of Mohammad Kabir, a low-income worker, died on November 6 and 8 while undergoing treatment at Chittagong Mother and Child Hospital after suffering from measles, dengue and pneumonia.
Their deaths come amid an alarming rise in infections, with health authorities reporting 1,318 deaths among children with confirmed or suspected measles since March 15, while dengue has claimed 502 lives this year.
Together, the two diseases have accounted for 1,820 reported deaths across their respective surveillance periods, although the figures cannot establish how many patients suffered from both infections.
Medical experts say measles can weaken the immune system and cause pneumonia and respiratory distress, while dengue can introduce additional complications, making treatment particularly challenging.
However, they caution that evidence remains insufficient to establish whether measles-related immune suppression directly increases dengue severity.
Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
At Bangladesh Shishu Hospital and Institute in Dhaka, doctors have encountered children diagnosed with both diseases, although the hospital does not maintain separate statistics on co-infections.
Professor Dr Atiqul Islam, a paediatric infectious disease specialist at the hospital, said children suffering from measles could develop serious respiratory complications.
“If dengue is contracted in addition to this, the patient's condition can become even more complex,” he said.
He explained that patients were generally treated in the ward where they were initially admitted, although separate accommodation could be arranged when necessary.
Hospital records show that 3,809 patients with measles or measles-like symptoms were admitted between January and November 16, with 106 deaths recorded.
During the same period, 950 dengue patients were admitted, seven of whom died.
At the capital's Infectious Diseases Hospital, 54 deaths associated with measles have been recorded this year.
The hospital has admitted 2,968 patients with measles-like symptoms and 744 confirmed measles patients, alongside treating 195 dengue patients.
Hospital superintendent Dr FA Asma Khan said managing simultaneous infections was particularly difficult among children with weakened immunity.
“When two diseases coexist, complications arise,” she said.
Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
Four-year-old Alif from Muradnagar in Comilla initially developed fever, body aches and vomiting before testing positive for dengue.
After his dengue symptoms improved, a rash appeared, and doctors subsequently diagnosed him with measles.
His mother said he had been receiving treatment for around 20 days, initially in Comilla and later at the Infectious Diseases Hospital in Dhaka.
Doctors have since reported an improvement in his condition and indicated that he could soon be discharged.
At Bangladesh Shishu Hospital, one-year-old Sukta from Kishoreganj is undergoing treatment for measles.
Her mother, Nilufa, said the child had developed a widespread rash and mouth sores, leaving her unable to eat and requiring intravenous fluids.
Nilufa's older son had previously recovered from measles after treatment at the same hospital.
Photo: Abir Ahmmed Shupto/Dhaka Tribune
Former Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research director Professor Dr Mahmudur Rahman said simultaneous circulation of infectious diseases increased the possibility of patients contracting more than one illness.
Public health expert Dr Mushtaq Hossain warned that measles and dengue had become major challenges for the country's health system.
He urged authorities to strengthen vaccination, mosquito control and infection prevention, while investigating why children were contracting measles despite vaccination.
According to the Directorate General of Health Services, four children with suspected measles died in the 24 hours reported on November 16.
During that period, 1,682 new suspected or confirmed measles cases were reported, including 173 laboratory-confirmed infections.
Since March 15, authorities have recorded 249,569 suspected measles cases, including 25,442 confirmed infections.
Experts emphasise that measles vaccination, destruction of Aedes mosquito breeding sites and coordinated disease surveillance are essential to reducing the risk of further infections.

item.title: Dhaka extortion attacks: Gunfire, arson hit businesses
item.description:
Around 11pm on Friday, bullets pierced the glass of Anurag Pharmacy, opposite the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases in the capital.
They passed over the head of employee Moin Uddin. He narrowly escaped death.
Allegations are that two criminals had demanded Tk50 lakh in extortion money from the pharmacy’s owner. When it was not paid, two rounds of crude bomb explosions came first. Then they opened fire.
On Sunday, more businesses were hit. Vehicles and a warehouse of AJR Courier Service were attacked in Mohammadpur and Hazaribagh. Two people were shot at the office of an internet service provider in Rampura.
Law enforcement agencies have intensified operations based on a list of 545 extortionists and criminals in the capital. Yet questions are being raised about why the armed dominance of extortionists is not stopping despite ongoing arrest operations.
Who will be targeted next?
It was around 11pm on Friday. Employee Moin Uddin was serving customers at Anurag Pharmacy, beside the main road towards Shyamoli, opposite the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases in the capital. Suddenly, the sound of gunfire shook the surrounding area. Before those present could understand what was happening, a second round of shots was fired. The bullets pierced the glass of the pharmacy and passed over Moin Uddin’s head. He narrowly escaped death.
Allegations have surfaced that two criminals known as ‘Killer Badal’ and ‘Killer Pappu’ demanded Tk50 lakh in extortion money from the owner of the pharmacy. After failing to receive the money, they first carried out two rounds of crude bomb explosions. They then opened fire directly.
Not just Anurag Pharmacy, incidents of gunfire, attacks, vandalism and arson targeting business establishments over extortion demands are taking place in various parts of the capital. On Sunday (November 15), vehicles and a warehouse of AJR Courier Service were attacked in Mohammadpur and Hazaribagh. On the same evening, two people were shot at the office of an internet service provider in Rampura.
These incidents, occurring one after another, are increasing concern among businesspeople. Allegations are that criminals are initially threatening businesses over the phone to collect extortion money. If their demands are not met, they are creating panic through crude bomb explosions, gunfire or arson. In this situation, law enforcement agencies have intensified operations based on a list of 545 extortionists and criminals in the capital.
Alongside Anurag Pharmacy, there are several other business establishments under the same name, including a restaurant and a supershop. The owner of these establishments is Syed Hasan Noor Islam Raston. He is known as a former councillor and Awami League leader. It has been learnt that he has been outside the country since the political changeover on August 5, 2024.
According to sources concerned, two criminals from the Mohammadpur area, Killer Badal and Killer Pappu, recently demanded Tk50 lakh in extortion money from Raston. After failing to receive the money, they carried out two rounds of crude bomb explosions targeting Anurag Pharmacy. They then opened fire there on Friday night.
Police said two people have already been arrested in connection with the shooting at the pharmacy. Efforts are underway to identify and arrest others involved in the attack.
The name of a criminal known as ‘Guja Badsha’ has recently come into discussion over allegations of extortion in the Rampura and Hatirjheel areas of the capital. He is known as a close associate of slain criminal Kailla Palash.
According to local sources, Guja Badsha’s influence in the area has increased since Kailla Palash was killed in a shooting in June this year. Earlier, he was arrested in April in the murder case of former police ASP Fazlul Haque. He was later released on bail. Allegations are that his followers are active in collecting extortion money from various business establishments, including cable television and internet connections, housing, garment factories and hotels in Rampura and Hatirjheel.
Most recently, on Sunday (November 15) evening, four to five young men entered the office of ‘Speed Touch Network and Technology’ on Wapda Road in Rampura and opened fire. Two people were injured. It has been learnt that two of the attackers were wearing masks on their faces and caps on their heads.
Bandon Kumar Saha, the company’s network operations in-charge, who brought the injured to the hospital, said: “15 to 20 days ago, Tk10 lakh in extortion money was demanded over mobile phones by people identifying themselves as Guja Badsha and Joni. They also threatened that they would not be allowed to do business in the area if the money was not paid. The shooting took place after that. We are living in great fear.”
According to sources at Rampura and Hatirjheel police stations, Guja Badsha has a total of 14 cases against him under the charges of murder, extortion, the Special Powers Act and the Explosives Act.
AJR Courier Service has been facing a series of attacks over an extortion dispute. Officials of the company allege that since October 18, there have been at least 20 incidents of attacks, vandalism and arson targeting its offices, warehouses and goods-carrying vehicles in Dhaka and Narayanganj over a period of nearly one month.
People associated with the company allege that a group had been demanding Tk20 lakh in extortion money and rent for the warehouse in Hazaribagh using the name of top criminal Sanjidul Islam Emon, also known as Captain Emon. The attacks began after the demands were not met.
On the night of October 18, threats were made to take over AJR’s office at a location in Hazaribagh rented from Bay Group. Two days later, on the evening of October 20, the company’s main warehouse near Sikder Medical College was attacked and looted.
Most recently, on Sunday, three covered vans belonging to AJR were stopped and vandalised in the Board Guard area of Beribadh in Mohammadpur. The attackers beat up the drivers and made it clear that the vehicles would not be allowed to leave until a settlement was reached with their ‘big brother’.
On the same night, 20 to 30 armed miscreants attacked AJR’s warehouse adjacent to Hazaribagh Beribadh. Alongside vandalising and looting the office, they opened fire and set two vehicles on fire. The company has filed several cases and general diaries at different police stations, including Hazaribagh, Mohammadpur and Shahbagh, over these incidents. Around 20 people have been arrested on suspicion of involvement in the attacks during law enforcement operations.
Jayanta Chowdhury, assistant general manager of the human resources and audit department of AJR Courier Service, said: “The attackers are identifying themselves as Captain Emon. However, we do not know who is actually behind this. As the main masterminds have not been arrested, the attacks on our company are not stopping either.”
According to intelligence information from various departments of law enforcement agencies, five crime-prone areas of the capital are under special surveillance. These are Mohammadpur, Mirpur, Badda, Jatrabari and Dhanmondi. Among these, Mohammadpur has been identified as the most vulnerable area, sources concerned said.
According to intelligence sources, multiple groups operating in the names of top criminals are active in extortion and establishing dominance in these areas. In many cases, extortion demands and death threats are initially made over WhatsApp using foreign phone numbers. This is followed by incidents of attacks involving firearms or sharp weapons.
Sources in law enforcement agencies also claim that disputes have developed over control of areas and establishing dominance among several top criminals who were released from prison following the political changeover in August 2024. Clashes and murders have also taken place between rival groups over these disputes.
Government intelligence agencies have prepared a list of 545 people to control extortion and criminal activities in the capital. Following instructions from the Home Ministry, operations to arrest those on the list have been intensified. More than 50 people have already been arrested, according to sources in law enforcement agencies. Most recently, a former BNP ward president named Masum Khan was arrested from Mohammadpur. Police said his name is also on the list.
Additional Police Commissioner Md Shafiqul Islam, chief of the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said: “Operations have been underway for the past week since receiving the list. Around 50 people have already been arrested.”
He said those against whom cases were already filed are being shown arrested in the respective cases. If illegal firearms are recovered during operations, cases are being filed under the Arms Act. In cases where there are no existing cases against individuals, their detention under the Special Powers Act, 1974, is being considered. The list is also being updated regularly.
SRB spokesperson and Bangladesh Air Force Wing Commander MZM Intekhab Chowdhury said: “Operations against extortionists and criminals began immediately after receiving the intelligence list under the instructions of the Home Ministry. A significant number of criminals have already been arrested. Operations based on intelligence information are underway across the country, including in the capital.”
Mohammad Ibne Mizan, deputy commissioner of the Tejgaon division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, said: “Our regular operations to arrest extortionists and criminals are ongoing. Two people have been arrested in connection with the shooting at Anurag Pharmacy. Around 20 people have also been arrested in the AJR incidents. Several people have been identified in connection with the attack on the internet office in Hatirjheel. Operations are underway to arrest them.”
The police official also warned that no one involved in criminal activities would be spared.
However, the series of attacks has raised questions about why the armed dominance of extortionists is not stopping despite ongoing arrest operations. Questions are also being raised about whether arresting only the attackers on the ground is sufficient in cases involving gunfire at business establishments, arson targeting vehicles and public attacks. In particular, unless the masterminds behind these incidents, the sources of illegal firearms and the flow of extortion money are identified, ensuring the security of businesspeople in the capital could become difficult.

item.title: Rooppur’s first power may reach national grid this week
item.description:
Electricity may begin flowing experimentally from the first unit of the Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant to the national grid this week, with preparations underway. After completing the initial stage of production, authorities are gradually raising the reactor’s power capacity to generate around 300MW.
Commercial production, however, may take around another year, and the price of the plant’s electricity has not yet been finalized. The authorities could not say when it will be determined. No payment is required for electricity supplied on a trial basis.
On October 29, the Bangladesh Atomic Energy Regulatory Authority (BAERA) approved the next phase of work on the first unit, called Power Startup or C-Stage. The activity began at 12:03pm on October 30, with pressure and temperature inside the reactor being increased. This is preparing the heat required for electricity production and the start of the relevant equipment.
Plant officials said the C-Stage target is to gradually raise the reactor’s capacity to 25-30%. During this period, the functionality of the reactor, cooling system, turbine, generator, electricity supply and control systems will be tested. These tests will confirm whether the plant can be operated safely and stably at different capacities. Once capacity reaches 25-30%, it may be possible to generate around 300MW and supply it experimentally to the national grid.
A plant official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said: “Preparations are underway. Electricity may even be connected to the national grid tomorrow, Tuesday. However, since this is a technical matter, I am not saying this with certainty.”
BAERA Chairman Mahmudul Hasan recently said the entire process would be monitored after electricity was supplied experimentally to the grid, to check that everything was proceeding properly. After tests and monitoring confirmed there were no problems or defects, the plant would be formally inaugurated.
Asked when consumers would receive electricity from the plant, officials said various tests could continue for seven to eight months after experimental production begins. During this period, the plant’s equipment, safety systems and capacity to supply electricity to the national grid would be assessed.
Connecting the generator to the national grid, known technically as synchronization, is an important milestone. Officials said commercial production will not begin immediately after experimental production starts. It must first be confirmed that the plant is operating reliably at different capacities, and the necessary approvals must then be obtained before commercial operation.
Earlier, the first nuclear reaction took place at the first unit for the first time on October 11. Although there were plans to begin this activity in September, it was postponed after defects were detected during tests of the safety valve. The necessary tests were later completed and BAERA approval was obtained.
Although preparations for supply are progressing, the purchase price of the electricity has not yet been finalized. The Bangladesh Power Development Board’s (BPDB) initial estimate was Tk6.72 per unit. However, costs have increased because the plant could not begin production within the scheduled timeframe, and relevant officials believe this could raise the price to around Tk10.
The company formed for the plant has submitted a proposal to the BPDB for signing a Power Purchase Agreement (PPA). Several rounds of meetings have been held, but final discussions on price determination have not been completed.
BPDB Chairman Engineer Rezaul Karim said the board had sought detailed information on the plant’s project costs and operation and maintenance expenses. These details are being examined and reviewed, and the price will be determined afterwards.
Government power plants are operated under the cost-based method, meaning the price per unit of electricity is determined based on the cost of constructing the plant.
As part of preparations to launch the two units, nuclear fuel uranium is regularly arriving from Russia. Most recently, at around 5:30am on November 14, the fuel was transported to the project area on three specialized lorries under tight security. This is the fifth consignment for the second unit. Including one consignment brought for the first unit, six consignments have so far reached Rooppur.
The Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, under construction on the bank of the Padma River in Ishwardi upazila of Pabna, has two units with a capacity of 1,200MW each. Once both are fully operational, a total of 2,400MW will be added to the national grid. Russia’s contractor company Atomstroyexport is constructing the plant.
The current project cost is Tk138,686 crore, an increase of around Tk26,000 crore due to the depreciation of the taka against the dollar. The project duration has been extended until June 2028.

item.title: Awami League back on Gopalganj streets despite security clampdown
item.description:
Leaders and activists of the activities-banned Awami League reopened their party office and the mausoleum of Sheikh Mujibur Rahman in Tungipara on Monday, pledging to bring former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to Bangladesh, even as security forces intensified operations across Gopalganj following Sunday's widespread violence and vandalism.
The renewed political mobilisation came as normal life gradually resumed in the district town under heavy security, with Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) personnel patrolling in armoured vehicles and police stationed at key roads and government installations.
Around 11am, Awami League and Chhatra League activists gathered in Tungipara and marched to the local party office, where they hoisted the national flag and the party flag while singing the national anthem.
The procession, reportedly led by Tungipara municipal Chhatra League president Sheikh Ifti Zaman Pallab, subsequently entered Bangabandhu's mausoleum complex after opening three gates.
Participants took an oath to continue their movement until Sheikh Hasina returned to Bangladesh.
"We have come together with the singular goal of bringing former prime minister Sheikh Hasina back to the country," Pallab said.
He declared that the party office would again serve as a gathering place for activists and that a wider movement would be launched from Tungipara.
Speaking at a press briefing near the old launch terminal in Gopalganj town around 5:15pm, Dhaka Range DIG Md Mostafizur Rahman said approximately 2,000 security personnel had been deployed to maintain law and order.
The deployment included police, 10 platoons of BGB and personnel from the Special Reserve Battalion, Armed Police Battalion and Ansar.
He said several suspects had been arrested during operations following Sunday's violence but did not disclose the number.
No case had yet been filed in connection with the incidents, he added.
Checkposts have been established at entry points from neighbouring districts to prevent outsiders from entering Gopalganj to create disturbances.
Responding to questions about the reopening of the Awami League office and mausoleum, the DIG warned that police would take legal action against any unlawful activity.
The latest developments followed the transfer of Gopalganj Deputy Commissioner Md Arif-uz-Zaman and Superintendent of Police Md Habibullah.
Three officers-in-charge were also transferred to Kishoreganj district: Md Ayub Ali of Tungipara police station, Riad Mahmud of Kotalipara and Mahfuzur Rahman of Kashiani.
The transfers were announced in an order signed by Dhaka Range DIG Mostafizur Rahman on Sunday.
However, the DIG rejected suggestions that the SP had been withdrawn as a disciplinary measure, describing the transfer as part of the police's regular administrative process.
On Sunday, Awami League and affiliated activists staged armed processions across Gopalganj, vandalised public property and reportedly attacked political opponents' establishments.
The incidents included attacks on BNP leaders' homes, damage to police property and the burning of a Grameen Bank branch, according to local accounts.
Despite the unrest, residents began returning to their daily activities on Monday. Shops reopened, educational institutions resumed classes and public transport returned to the streets.
However, fear persisted among residents following the violence.

item.title: Doctors may receive Tk1,861cr a year in commissions for test referrals
item.description:
Doctors in Bangladesh receive commissions ranging from 20% to 50% of the fees for the respective tests by advising patients to undergo tests at various diagnostic centres, a study by Bangladesh Health Watch (BHW) has found.
According to the study’s calculations, transactions worth approximately Tk1,861 crore may take place annually in the country’s major diagnostic centres in the form of such commissions.
The report noted, however, that this figure needs to be independently verified.
The study also revealed widespread irregularities in the health sector, including doctors’ absence from government hospitals and irregularities in the purchase of medical equipment. Nearly 40% of doctors at government hospitals were not found at their workplaces during surprise inspections. The study also found financial losses of Tk459 crore in purchases by the Central Medical Stores Depot (CMSD) and medical equipment worth Tk283 crore lying unused. There were instances of equipment being purchased at prices 18 times higher than its market value.
These findings were presented on Sunday at the publication ceremony of BHW’s 2025-26 biennial report at the International Mother Language Institute in Dhaka. The 191-page report contains 11 chapters written by 17 researchers. It was edited by BHW Convener Dr Ahmed Mustaque Raza Chowdhury and Dr Shams El Arifeen, Emeritus Scientist at the International Centre for Diarrhoeal Disease Research, Bangladesh (icddr,b). The Embassy of Sweden and the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency (Sida) assisted in preparing the report.
Speaking at the ceremony, Dr Shams El Arifeen said weak governance, excessive decision-making powers without accountability, failure to control conflicts of interest, and lack of coordination in monitoring are mainly responsible for corruption in the health sector. The institutional tendency to accept irregularities as normal also plays a role in sustaining it, he said.
He said corruption cannot be eliminated through law enforcement alone, and that integrity and ethics must be developed as inseparable parts of institutional culture.
State Minister for Health MA Muhith said bringing those involved in corruption to justice alone would not solve the problem, and that necessary reforms must be made to the overall structure of the health sector. Alongside financial irregularities and manipulation of tenders, he said, influencing policies and strategies in the interests of a particular group also falls under corruption.
The report highlighted various irregularities and harassment faced by patients seeking treatment at government hospitals. These include being forced to obtain services through brokers, illegal payments for bed allocation and hospital discharge, and referrals to private clinics and diagnostic centres.
In one such incident, a hospital ward boy took Tk5,000 from an elderly patient by promising to arrange a date for surgery, though there were no arrangements for surgery in the relevant ward. Later, instead of disciplinary action being taken against the employee, he was transferred to another place.
The absence of doctors from government hospitals and health centres was identified as one of the biggest challenges in healthcare services. Besides the surprise inspections that found nearly 40% of doctors absent, another study found that absence rates at several health centres in remote areas exceeded 70%.
The report also highlighted the issue of receiving government salaries and allowances without performing duties. Researchers further identified political influence and weaknesses in the paper-based management system in the recruitment, transfer and promotion of more than 180,000 employees in the health sector. As an example, the report mentioned the cancellation of the recruitment of 2,839 health workers in 2021.
BHW also raised questions about the independence and accountability of regulatory institutions in the health sector. Of approximately 90 members of the Bangladesh Medical and Dental Council (BMDC), 70 are associated with the government. None of the six regulatory bodies reviewed has effective representation of patients or the general public.
The report found evidence of delays in resolving allegations of medical negligence. From 2010 to May 2025, a total of 172 complaints were submitted to the BMDC. Of these, 79 are still awaiting resolution, and disciplinary action has been taken in only 29 cases.
The report further stated that although the number of medical colleges has increased rapidly, from 62 in 2010 to 118 in 2022-23, sufficient measures have not been developed to ensure the quality of medical education. Quality control and monitoring systems have not improved accordingly.
To reduce corruption and irregularities, BHW has recommended making all information on government procurement publicly available and ensuring accountability at every stage, from the purchase of medical equipment to its use. It has also stressed the protection of those who disclose information about corruption.
To ensure the independence of regulatory bodies, the organisation has proposed preventing ministers, secretaries and members of parliament from becoming heads of these institutions. It has also recommended ensuring representation of patients and the general public in regulatory bodies, and establishing an independent mechanism for appeals against their decisions.

item.title: Community Bank, Suzuki-Rancon to expand motorcycle financing for police personnel
item.description:
Community Bank Bangladesh PLC has signed a memorandum of understanding with Suzuki-Rancon, the distributor of Suzuki motorcycles in Bangladesh, to make motorcycle ownership more accessible to members of Bangladesh Police.
Through the partnership, eligible personnel will be able to finance the purchase of a Suzuki motorcycle of their choice.
Mohammed Emtiaz Uddin, managing director and CEO of Community Bank Bangladesh PLC, and Habib Iftikher Alam, chief executive officer of Suzuki-Rancon, attended the signing ceremony on behalf of their respective organizations.
Eligible Bangladesh Police personnel will be able to access financing of up to Tk250,000 at an interest rate of 9%, with a repayment period of up to 10 years.
The facility will be available through the bank’s conventional and Islamic banking services.
The managing director and CEO’s vision for this partnership was to support the people who keep the public safe by making their everyday travel easier.
By helping police personnel spread the cost of owning a motorcycle, the bank aims to give them greater independence and flexibility in their working and family lives.
Better access to transport can benefit their families and the communities that rely on their service.
Since its inception, Community Bank has developed banking services around the financial needs of Bangladesh Police personnel.
This partnership builds on that commitment and reflects the bank’s broader aim of improving everyday life by making financial services more accessible to individuals, families and communities across Bangladesh.

item.title: Meherpur homemaker wins free appliances after buying Marcel Fridge
item.description:
A refrigerator purchase brought an unexpected windfall for Mosammat Lipiara, a housewife from Bamundi Union in Gangni upazila of Meherpur, as she received a houseful of free electronic appliances under Marcel's ongoing Digital Campaign Season-25.
Lipiara, who purchased a refrigerator from Marcel, one of the country's leading electronics brands, received a wide range of free products, including another refrigerator, air conditioner, television, washing machine, microwave oven, gas stove, infrared cooker, rice cooker, blender, ceiling fan, rechargeable fan, geyser, iron and electric kettle.
Popular model and film actor Irfan Sajjad and actress Prarthana Fardin Dighi formally handed over the gifts to Lipiara at a ceremony held at Bamundi Bazar in Meherpur on Sunday, November 15.
The event was organized by Taj Electronics, an authorized distributor of Marcel, to celebrate the handover of the gifts under the brand's nationwide promotional campaign.
Among others, Marcel deputy chief marketing officer Md Rabiul Alam Bhuiyan, Marcel distributor network’s sales captain Nurul Islam Rubel, Marcel Refrigerator brand manager Mostafizur Rahman, Taj Electronics proprietor Ziadul Islam Lijon, and local dignitaries attended the ceremony.
Marcel launched its nationwide Digital Campaign Season-25 on October 17, offering customers an opportunity to win a houseful of electronic appliances for free upon purchasing refrigerators, televisions, air conditioners or ceiling fans and completing digital registration.
The campaign, which will continue until December 31, 2026, also offers customers opportunities to win overseas trips, cashback and a range of guaranteed gifts.
As part of the campaign, Lipiara recently purchased a Marcel refrigerator from Taj Electronics at Bamundi Bazar.
Following the purchase, her details, including her name, mobile phone number and the refrigerator's barcode number, were registered in Marcel's digital system.
Shortly after completing the registration, Lipiara received an SMS on her registered mobile number informing her that she had won a houseful of free electronic appliances.
Expressing her excitement at the gift handover ceremony, Lipiara said: "I am truly delighted to have received a houseful of gifts as promised by Marcel. My entire family is overjoyed to receive so many valuable products, including an air conditioner, a television, a refrigerator, a washing machine and a microwave oven, simply by purchasing a Marcel fridge."
Speaking at the ceremony, actor Irfan Sajjad and actress Prarthana Fardin Dighi said the event demonstrated Marcel's commitment to fulfilling its promises to customers.
"Today's event is a clear example of how Marcel honours its commitments to ordinary customers. By delivering a houseful of free appliances to a customer, the brand has once again demonstrated its dedication to customer satisfaction," they said.
The two celebrities also encouraged consumers to purchase high-quality products from domestic brands like Marcel to support the sustainable growth of Bangladesh's local industries.
Popular comedian Abu Hena Rony, widely known for his performances on the comedy show Mirakkel, hosted the event and entertained the audience with his humorous performances.
The gift handover ceremony concluded with a cultural program.

item.title: Bus set on fire in Mirpur
item.description:
A bus of the Rajdhani Paribahan company was set on fire by unidentified individuals in Mirpur-1, Dhaka, at around 9:30pm on Monday.
Sihab, an on-duty official at the Fire Service and Civil Defence headquarters, confirmed the incident.

item.title: COP31 launches AI pledge, green industrialisation drive to accelerate climate action
item.description:
The COP31 Presidency has launched a series of initiatives to promote responsible artificial intelligence (AI), green industrialisation and climate technology, aiming to ensure that technological progress supports climate action rather than exacerbates emissions and inequality.
Announced in Antalya on Monday, the initiatives include the Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge, the AI-Enabled Cleantech Initiative and the Antalya Green Industrialisation Compact.
The package also includes the Least Developed Countries Green Industrialisation Facilitation (LDC-GIF) mechanism, which aims to help developing countries access technology, investment and financial support for low-emission industrial development.
The announcements come amid growing concerns over the environmental footprint of AI, particularly the rising electricity and water consumption of data centres and their potential reliance on fossil fuels.
Addressing these concerns, UN Secretary-General António Guterres warned that the benefits of AI must outweigh its growing environmental and social costs, stressing that technology companies must take responsibility for their increasing energy consumption and emissions.
He said the rapid expansion of data centres was putting additional pressure on electricity systems, potentially increasing pollution and driving up electricity costs for households and businesses.
He cautioned that meeting the additional electricity demand through fossil fuels could undermine global climate goals.
Guterres also warned against technology companies setting up gas-fired power plants at data centre facilities to bypass electricity grid constraints, saying that shifting fossil fuel generation off the grid would not eliminate the resulting emissions.
He called on technology companies to align their business and investment strategies with the Paris Agreement, set credible climate targets, improve energy efficiency and disclose their energy and water consumption.
He also urged companies to power data centres with renewable energy and ensure that additional clean electricity generation keeps pace with rising demand without shifting infrastructure costs onto consumers.
"AI's benefits must outweigh its growing costs. And those benefits must reach every country," he said.
Guterres further warned that AI must not fuel disinformation, undermine scientific research, deepen social divisions or concentrate wealth.
He stressed that affected communities must have a meaningful voice in decisions about data centres, particularly regarding their impact on local water resources, electricity bills and the environment.
At the High-Level Green Digital Action Roundtable, the COP31 Presidency introduced the Antalya Artificial Intelligence Pledge, a voluntary framework inviting governments, companies and organisations to commit to responsible AI development and deployment in support of climate action.
The pledge identifies four priority areas: sustainable energy and infrastructure for AI systems; responsible AI design and management throughout its lifecycle; assessment and disclosure of environmental impacts; and financial and technical support for AI-driven climate solutions, particularly in developing countries, least developed countries and Small Island Developing States.
Potential commitments include disclosing energy and water consumption, powering AI infrastructure with low-emission electricity, adopting green data centre standards, developing resource-efficient AI systems and promoting circular economy practices to reduce electronic waste.
The framework also encourages investment in computing capacity, technical skills and AI-based climate solutions in countries with limited technological capacity.
International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Secretary-General Doreen Bogdan-Martin said AI could become a powerful tool for tackling the climate crisis but must be developed and deployed responsibly.
"The Antalya AI Pledge galvanizes international action towards sustainable, accountable AI innovation that benefits everyone, especially the most climate-vulnerable nations," she said.
Guterres said AI could deliver significant climate benefits if its development focused on practical solutions, particularly for vulnerable communities and developing countries.
Potential applications include improving electricity grid efficiency, integrating more wind and solar power, strengthening climate-risk assessments and helping communities prepare for extreme weather events.
AI-powered early warning systems could give families more time to prepare for floods, while satellite information and local data could help farmers anticipate droughts and adapt their agricultural practices.
However, he warned that developing countries must not be left behind because of limited access to finance, computing infrastructure and reliable data. He also highlighted the UN Climate Change AI for Climate Action Award, which recognises and promotes technology-driven climate solutions.
This year's winner, CLIMAID, developed by Tanzania's Upendo Ernest Lyimo, combines artificial intelligence, satellite information and local data to support climate-risk assessments and adaptation planning.
Guterres stressed that developing countries must have a role in shaping AI's future and sharing its benefits.
Alongside the AI initiatives, the COP31 Presidency is promoting green industrialisation as a key component of global efforts to cut emissions while supporting economic development.
Industry accounts for around a quarter of global greenhouse gas emissions, making the transition to near-zero and low-emission production essential to meeting climate targets.
The Antalya Green Industrialisation Compact aims to accelerate investment, implementation and technology deployment while recognising that countries and industries have different starting points, economic conditions and development priorities.
The initiative seeks to promote industrial electrification, improve energy and resource efficiency and expand the production of cleaner technologies.
COP31 President Murat Kurum said industrial development and technological innovation must become integral to climate solutions.
"Industry and technology must be part of the climate solution. We need to electrify industry, adapted to the starting point and strategic choices of each country," he said.
He added that the rapid expansion of AI must be powered and deployed responsibly and directed towards climate action.
According to Kurum, AI and clean technologies could help businesses, including energy-intensive manufacturers and agricultural enterprises, sustain economic growth without a corresponding increase in material and energy consumption.
UNIDO Director General Gerd Mueller said countries should not have to choose between economic development and climate action.
"Green industrialization is key to reducing emissions while building the clean technology industries, skills and quality jobs of the future in every region," he said.
The LDC-GIF mechanism, presented on November 12, aims to address barriers that prevent least developed countries from developing and implementing green industrial projects.
It combines project development, technology matching and transfer, institutional capacity-building and access to existing financing opportunities.
The mechanism operates under the secretariat of the UN Technology Bank for Least Developed Countries, which is hosted by Türkiye.
Meanwhile, the COP31 Presidency, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the Climate Club, an intergovernmental forum comprising 50 countries, issued guidance on country platforms for industrial transformation on November 12.
The guidance aims to help countries turn industrial policy objectives into investment-ready projects by improving governance, investment conditions, project pipelines, financing and monitoring mechanisms.
The COP31 Presidency and the ITU, in collaboration with UN-Habitat and the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), will also launch a call to action on using AI, digital twins and the Internet of Things (IoT) to accelerate climate action in cities.
The initiative invites governments, municipalities, businesses, universities and international organisations to expand the use of these technologies to develop smarter, more climate-resilient urban areas.
Together, the initiatives support the COP31 Presidency's 35-by-35 ambition to raise electricity's share of final energy consumption to 35% by 2035.
As the climate summit enters its second week, COP31 President of Negotiations Chris Bowen has urged countries to keep scientific evidence at the centre of negotiations.
Bowen said climate science must guide discussions on emissions reductions, adaptation and the next global stocktake.
"The latest science tells us that we will overshoot the 1.5-degree goal, but science also shows that we can return to safer temperatures if we work together and act with urgency," he said.
He also stressed the importance of maintaining scientific evidence as a foundation for international climate commitments and implementation.
Research by Professor Johan Rockström on overshooting the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C temperature limit, presented on Monday, was highlighted as an important contribution to the discussions.
Bowen said countries must continue working together to cut emissions and strengthen adaptation efforts despite the growing risk of temporarily exceeding the global temperature threshold.
Guterres also stressed that the energy transition must not proceed at two different speeds, with technologically advanced economies benefiting disproportionately while developing countries struggle to access affordable solutions.
He said AI must help bridge this divide by supporting affordable, efficient technologies tailored to the needs of vulnerable communities.
The initiatives announced at COP31 seek to establish a framework in which technological progress, industrial development and climate responsibility advance together.
However, their success will ultimately depend on whether voluntary commitments translate into measurable emissions reductions, affordable clean energy and tangible benefits for developing countries.

item.title: Rajshahi farmers reap bumper Aman harvest, but low prices sour the mood
item.description:
Farmers in Rajshahi are enjoying a bumper Aman harvest this season, with yields reaching 17–20 maunds per bigha in some areas thanks to favourable weather. However, their joy is being dampened by low market prices, with paddy selling for just Tk1,200 per maund.
Rising costs of fertiliser, pesticides, diesel and labour have pushed up production expenses, leaving farmers worried about their returns. They say paddy should fetch at least Tk1,400–1,500 per maund to cover costs and ensure a reasonable profit.
Harvesting of early-maturing transplanted Aman varieties began in different parts of the district in early November. The Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) expects harvesting to gain pace over the next one to two weeks.
During a visit to the Teghor, Bagsara and Paikpara fields in Nawhata municipality of Paba upazila on Monday morning, vast stretches of farmland were seen covered with ripe and partially ripe golden paddy. Farmers were busy harvesting, bundling and threshing the crop, while their families were preparing to bring the harvest home.
Local farmers said early-maturing BRRI-103 and BINA-17 varieties had produced good yields this year. Some have already completed harvesting and sold their produce. However, higher production costs have raised concerns about profitability. Many are preparing their fields for potatoes, winter vegetables and pulses after harvesting Aman.
Mamun Rashid of Teghor village cultivated BRRI-103 Aman on three bighas, harvesting 20 maunds per bigha.
He said land preparation, planting and fertiliser application cost Tk7,000 per bigha, while harvesting, threshing, transportation and labour expenses added another Tk7,000. This brought the total production cost to Tk14,000 per bigha on his own land. Cultivation on leased or sharecropped land requires an additional Tk5,000.
Mamun said he sold 20 maunds of paddy at Nawhata market on Sunday for Tk1,200 per maund, earning Tk24,000. After deducting production costs, his return from paddy was Tk10,000 per bigha.
He also harvested around 21 bundles of straw per bigha, selling each for Tk250 and earning another Tk5,250. Including straw sales, his surplus came to around Tk15,250 per bigha.
He is now preparing the land for potato cultivation.
Munzur Rahman, a farmer from Bagsara Beel, cultivated BINA-17 Aman on 10 bighas at a production cost of Tk17,000 per bigha. His average yield was 18 maunds.
He recently sold 20 maunds at Tk1,200 each but has kept the remaining paddy in the hope of better prices. After accounting for all expenses and income from straw sales, he said he made a profit of around Tk10,000 per bigha.
Shahidul Islam of Paikpara, who cultivated BRRI-51 Aman on three bighas of leased land, expects to begin harvesting next week.
He said fertiliser, pesticide and diesel prices, as well as labour wages, had increased compared with last year.
"At Tk1,200 per maund, farmers cannot make a reasonable profit. The price needs to be at least Tk1,500 to make cultivation worthwhile," he said.
Yusuf Ali, another farmer from Paba, cultivated BRRI-10 Aman on five bighas of sharecropped land. He has already harvested two bighas, with an average yield of 18 maunds per bigha.
He said the harvest had been good and the crop had been brought in on time, but sharecroppers would not benefit unless they received a fair price.
According to the Rajshahi DAE, the cultivation target for transplanted Aman this season was 83,600 hectares. Farmers have cultivated 83,670 hectares, exceeding the target by 70 hectares.
The district's total production target has been set at 314,336 tonnes. So far, harvesting has been completed on 12,423 hectares, while the targeted average yield is 17–20 maunds per bigha.
Godagari leads the district in Aman cultivation, with 23,762 hectares, followed by Tanore with 22,071 hectares, Paba with 9,140 hectares, Durgapur with 5,645 hectares, Charghat with 5,450 hectares, Mohanpur with 4,100 hectares, Bagmara with 3,725 hectares and Bagha with 2,352 hectares.
Bagha Upazila Agriculture Officer MA Mannan said Aman had been cultivated on 2,352 hectares in the upazila this season, with an average yield of around 20 maunds per bigha.
Rajshahi DAE Deputy Director Mostafa Kamal Hossain said harvesting had been completed on 12,423 hectares and full-scale harvesting was expected to begin within the next one to two weeks.
He attributed the good yield to favourable weather and a lower incidence of pests and diseases.
He added that farmers were preparing to cultivate potatoes, mustard, maize, wheat and winter vegetables on the same land after harvesting early Aman, creating opportunities for multiple cropping.
The government has decided to procure paddy at fair prices to support farmers, he said, adding that the agriculture department would also monitor the market to help ensure farmers receive reasonable prices.

item.title: Dhaka to host 51st ICQCC from November 18
item.description:
The 51st International Convention on Quality Control Circles (ICQCC-2026) will be held in Dhaka from November 18 to 20 under the theme “QCC for Sustainable Development.”
The Bangladesh Society for Total Quality Management (BSTQM) and the University of Asia Pacific (UAP) are jointly organizing the convention. Around 8,000 members of approximately 800 Quality Control Circle (QCC) teams from 16 countries and regions are expected to participate.
Details of the convention were shared at a press conference held at Pan Pacific Sonargaon Dhaka on Sunday. Those present included BSTQM President and ICQCC-2026 Convener A K M Shamsul Huda, BSTQM Adviser Engr. A M M Khairul Bashar, UAP Registrar Brig Gen (Retd) Prof Dr A K M Nazrul Islam, BSTQM Secretary General M M Kabir, and ICQCC-2026 Technical and Evaluation Committee Member Md Rokibul Islam, along with representatives of BSTQM and UAP and members of the media.
Of the participating teams, 141 will present onsite and 652 online. The main presentation sessions will be held at UAP on November 19 and 20, where teams will showcase workplace improvement projects focusing on productivity, quality enhancement, cost reduction and problem-solving.
Nearly 100 local and international judges will evaluate the presentations.
Participating countries and regions include Japan, China, India, South Korea, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Sri Lanka, the Philippines, Taiwan, Namibia, Zambia, Mozambique and Mauritius, along with Bangladesh.
ICQCC is coordinated internationally by the Union of Japanese Scientists and Engineers (JUSE) of Japan and is known as the “Quality Olympics.” It is one of the world's largest annual platforms for promoting QCC and Total Quality Management (TQM).
Bangladesh is hosting the convention for the third time.
The convention will conclude on November 20 with the announcement of results, a prize-giving ceremony and the formal handover of the ICQCC flag to the Philippines, host of the next convention.
